page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.8-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, providing 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with dedicated compute resource isolation.

The virtual machine includes 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage volumes, requiring external networked block storage for operating system persistence and application data. There are no discrete GPU accelerators available on this shape. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance, the configuration represents a standard resource density model without asymmetric memory or compute weighting. It is technically suited for general enterprise applications, mid-tier web serving, microservices architectures, build environments, and containerized backend services that rely on remote storage solutions.

The hardware configuration supplies 64.0 GB of memory, delivering an even allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance. Due to its balanced compute-to-memory profile, this virtual machine suits general enterprise application hosting, middle-tier web servers, microservice workloads, and continuous integration pipelines operating with detached storage.
